request.spec:
The screen gains a header with counters, shown at all times: the number of people on the sheet
(retired people included), the number of claims in each status (DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING, SETTLED,
VOID), the sheet's due-total and the sheet's overdue-total. Each counter always equals the figure
it repeats: the status counts those of the summary, the two totals the sheet's totals.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The screen gains a header with counters, shown at all times: the number of people on the sheet
(retired people included), the number of claims in each status (DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING, SETTLED,
VOID), the sheet's due-total and the sheet's overdue-total. Each counter always equals the figure
it repeats: the status counts those of the summary, the two totals the sheet's totals.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The screen now has a header with the counters, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**What the header shows.** It sits at the top of the sheet: the people count (retired people included), a count for each claim status (DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING, SETTLED, VOID), the sheet's due-total and its overdue-total. It's a new file, `features/header/header.slot.tsx`, set to render before every other panel.

**Why the counters can't drift.** The header doesn't do its own sums. The status counts and the sheet totals each come from one shared function in `features/claims/claims.ts`:
- `CLAIM_STATUSES` / `statusCount` give the per-status counts, now used by both the summary and the header.
- `useSheetTotals` gives the claimed-total, due-total and overdue figures, moved out of the rollup panel. The rollup panel and the header both use it now.

So each header counter is worked out the same way as the figure it repeats elsewhere.

Only the front end changed. The figures could already be worked out from data the screen loads, so the stored data, server and audit records are untouched. The header only appears once a sheet is loaded, because every count belongs to a sheet.
